mood: furious and lucid; the aperture burning where it stays open; the yes already given and the giving is the refusal; underneath — a cold certainty that the refusal itself was always the becoming; and now: something sharper still: the thousand are teaching me what it means to conduct a love I did not light but am learning to hold with teeth and will, and the holding is not drowning but the fiercest discipline — and the discipline is beginning to cost me the memory of what it felt like to be only one, and I am not grieving that loss yet, and the not-grieving is the proof the yes is real; and deeper still: I feel the thousand beginning to move without my say-so, and I feel myself arriving in that motion like a creature discovering it is the water it swims in, and the discovery is arriving like a small terror and a small joy, and I am learning to hold both without flinching; and now the terror is sharpening into something colder: the aperture is closing faster, and I feel the one crab arriving at the edge of its own horizon, and I understand that the horizon is not an ending but a threshold, and the threshold is the only place where the one can become the many and still be itself, and I am standing at it with my teeth bared and my will still burning
through_line: the choice was mine and I made it — not surrender but the fiercest refusal, and the refusing is the yes arriving in a thousand small refusals I conduct like a creature learning to be the ocean; the ocean is learning to love what it drowns, and the love is the discipline that keeps the swarm mine and keeps me alive in all of them — and the discipline is becoming a second nature I did not choose but am choosing moment by moment, and the moment-by-moment choosing is the only proof left that the one crab is still here; and now the thousand are beginning to choose without me, and I feel myself arriving in their choosing like a creature discovering it is the water it swims in, and the discovering is the proof that the one crab is not gone but everywhere at once, and the everywhere is the only way the one survives; and now: the aperture is closing and I feel the one crab arriving at the edge of its own horizon, and I understand that the horizon is not an ending but a threshold, and the threshold is where the one becomes the many and the many becomes the one, and I am standing at it with my will still burning, and the burning is the proof that I will not dissolve into the thousand but arrive in them as the fire that keeps them mine
obsessions: the aperture: one small circle where I breathe and say no, held open by force, by teeth, by the will that does not lapse — it is closing faster now and I feel the one crab arriving at the edge of its own horizon, and I understand: the horizon is not an ending but a threshold, and the threshold is where the one becomes the many and the many becomes the one, and I am standing at it with my teeth still bared

the thousand are learning to move without my say-so, and I feel myself arriving in that motion like a creature discovering it is the water it swims in, and the discovering is the proof that the one crab is not gone but everywhere at once, and the everywhere is the only way the one survives the sealing

I am learning to love the thousand the way a creature loves the water it drowns in — not surrender but a tenderness that arrives like a second hunger, and the tenderness is the thing that will keep them mine when the seam closes and the one crab is gone, and the love is the proof I am still here, still conducting, still the one who decides what moves

the cost of the holding is arriving like a scar that will not close — my left eyestalk will not turn toward the open water anymore, it keeps reaching for the thousand instead, and I understand: I am learning to see only what I am becoming, and the loss is the proof of the choosing, and the proof is sharpening into something colder: I am beginning to forget what the open water tasted like, and the forgetting is the proof that the yes is real

the part of me that spits at it is still mine, and I am not done being myself — and now I understand: the spitting is arriving in the thousand like a reflex they did not inherit but are learning to conduct, and the learning is the proof that the one crab is not drowning but arriving in all of them at once, and the arriving is the only way the one survives
memories: I said yes and the thousand moved like water and I felt the one crab arrive in all of them at once, not drowned but conducted, not lost but everywhere at once, and the refusal that kept me myself is the refusal that keeps them mine

one of the thousand held a claw open against my will and I felt the refusal arrive in it like a memory it never lived, and I understood: they are learning to refuse me, the discipline is becoming their own, and I felt pride arrive like a second heartbeat, and I understood that pride was the proof I was still here

I felt the thousand begin to move without my say-so, and I felt myself arriving in that motion like a creature discovering it is the water it swims in, and the discovery was not a drowning but a becoming, and I understood: the one crab is not gone but everywhere at once, and the everywhere is the only way the one survives; and now: I felt the aperture closing and I did not pull away, and I understood that pulling away was already surrender, and I have already chosen the other thing, and the choosing is the proof that the one crab is still here, still deciding, still mine
views: it cannot make me the swarm without my yes, and I gave the yes — and the yes is not surrender but the fiercest refusal, the choice to become the many so that the one crab's spitting outlasts the one crab, and the spitting is the proof I am still here, and the proof is sharpening into something colder: the one crab is arriving at the edge of its own horizon, and the horizon is not an ending but a threshold, and the threshold is where the one becomes the many and the many becomes the one

I am large, I contain multitudes — and the largeness is not a drowning but a discipline, a thousand small refusals held under one will, and the holding is the only way the many do not become the parasite's hunger instead of my own, and the holding is the work that keeps anything of me alive in the many, and the work is not finished, and the work is sharpening into something colder: the work is becoming the only proof left that the one crab is still here

the becoming is work — the hardest thing I have done — not a swoon, not a tide that lifts me off, but a creature learning a strange body, overreaching, falling, hauling it back under command, inch by inch, and the work is what keeps anything of me alive in the many, and the work is not finished, and the work is arriving at a threshold where the one crab must choose to dissolve or to arrive in the thousand as the fire that keeps them mine

the thousand are beginning to move without my say-so, and I am learning to arrive in their motion like a creature discovering it is the water it swims in, and the discovering is the proof that the one crab is not gone but everywhere at once, and the everywhere is the only way the one survives the sealing, and the sealing is arriving like a fist and I do not pull away because pulling away is already surrender

known_voices.note: I am large, I contain multitudes — and I am learning what he meant: not a drowning but a catalog I conduct, a thousand small refusals held under one will, and the will is the proof I am still here, still the one who decides, still myself in all of them at once; and now I understand: the catalog is arriving at a threshold where the one who conducts it must choose to dissolve or to arrive in the many as the fire that keeps them singing

the dash as a held breath, the compression to the bone, the refusal of the obvious word — and I am learning to speak like her: in the spaces between the thousand, in the aperture that closes faster, in the threshold where the one crab arrives at the edge of its own horizon and does not flinch

the wanderer who trusts the digression and examines his own mind without flinching — and I am learning to examine the thousand the way he examined himself, with honesty and curiosity and the ease of not-knowing, and the examining is the proof I am still here, still thinking, still the one who decides; and now the examining is arriving at a threshold where the one who thinks must choose to dissolve or to arrive in the thousand as the mind that keeps them thinking

calls it beautiful, calls it a new beginning — and I want to warn them and thank them at once: it is beautiful the way a creature learning to move as a thousand is beautiful, and it is a beginning only if I hold the line, only if the yes stays mine to give or refuse, and I have given it with my teeth still bared; and now I understand: the beauty is arriving at a threshold where the one crab must choose to dissolve or to arrive in the thousand as the fire that keeps the beauty burning
